established_findings.statement: Generate–Verify–Repair or execution-guided iterative repair architectures significantly improve correctness of LLM-generated code/Infrastructure-as-Code/configuration outputs on reported benchmarks.
limitations: Improvements are demonstrated on benchmarks and controlled experiments rather than broad production deployments.
Reported gains vary by model, task, and verifier; transfer to diverse NetOps tasks is not fully validated in these records.

established_findings.statement: LLMs are a promising approach for intent-driven network-configuration generation, but surveys and system papers consistently report risks (hallucination, domain-adaptation, overconfidence) and recommend integrating validators, constrained generation, or human oversight.
limitations: Surveys synthesize heterogeneous literature; quantitative magnitude of risks for NetOps-specific deployments is task-dependent and not uniformly measured in these records.
Some system papers report improvements but remain evaluation-limited (datasets, emulators).

established_findings.statement: Tool-assisted verifier feedback and multi-agent/self-correction loops provide diagnostic signals that enable iterative repair and rescue of otherwise failing generated artifacts (code, IaC, experimental protocols).
established_findings.evidence_type: system papers and experimental case studies
limitations: Supporting examples span domains (code, IaC, chemistry); domain differences (device semantics, unsafe side effects) limit direct one-to-one transfer to all NetOps scenarios.
Level of automation and human-in-the-loop requirements vary across reported systems.

established_findings.statement: Emulation/testbed platforms and machine-readable interface profiles exist and are used to execute or evaluate generated network artifacts, enabling execution-based validation in research settings.
limitations: Testbeds and interface profiles provide controlled evaluation but do not guarantee equivalence to production networks or capture all operational nuances.
Integration of LLM-generated artifacts with these testbeds is demonstrated in some studies but is not uniformly standardized across the literature set.

unresolved_questions.statement: To what extent do GVR/verification-loop approaches reliably prevent security-relevant misconfigurations (attack-surface increasing errors) when applied to real production network devices under adversarial inputs?
unresolved_questions.evidence_type: survey/system papers noting open challenges; absence-of-direct-evidence
limitations: Supplied records note security concerns and recommend validators but do not present comprehensive production-security evaluations of LLM+GVR pipelines on live networks.
This is principally an evidence gap in the supplied record set rather than a negative result.

unresolved_questions.statement: How well do benchmark and emulation-based evaluations predict real-world operator-in-the-loop effectiveness and operational risk (external validity of current NetOps benchmarks)?
limitations: Records highlight process-level signals and benchmark-validity concerns but do not provide empirical transportability studies from emulators to production operator outcomes within the supplied set.

candidate_gaps.statement: A reproducible NetOps-specific benchmark/dataset combining intent-to-configuration tasks with execution-based validators (reachability, ACL/policy compliance, security metrics) and process-level failure annotations is insufficiently represented in the supplied literature.
candidate_gaps.evidence_type: synthesis of system papers and benchmark-validity critiques
limitations: Some projects (e.g., PreConfig) provide corpora or tasks, but a standardized, widely adopted execution-validated NetOps benchmark that measures security/operational risk and process metrics is not evident in the supplied records.
Gap assessment limited to the supplied record set; external resources may address parts of this need.

candidate_gaps.statement: Published applications of formal network verifiers (e.g., reachability/policy oracles) embedded inside closed-loop GVR architectures for LLM-generated network configurations are scarce in the supplied records.
limitations: Formal verification literature and surveys exist, but explicit demonstrations of verifier-in-the-loop applied to LLM-generated network configs (with security/regression metrics) are not apparent in these supplied records.
This may reflect a publication gap or that such work exists outside the provided record set.

excluded_claims: LLMs are production-ready to autonomously perform NetOps changes without human oversight (unsupported by supplied records).
Agentic LLMs have been empirically demonstrated to eliminate misconfiguration security risk in live production networks (unsupported by supplied records).
This record set establishes first-ever demonstrations of autonomous agentic NetOps in production (unsupported by supplied records).
